# Framework Complexity @ Stage 10 — Concrete Peak

> developed 2026-07-24.

## Crosswalk (from unified ladder)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IST Stage# | 10 |
| Canonical name | Concrete Peak |
| Altitude | `amber` (Ethnocentric) |
| MHC Order | 9 (Concrete) |
| Kegan | 3 |
| Identity band | Ethnocentric |

## Expression on this line

Framework complexity at Stage 10 achieves **complex framework coordination** — the capacity to
coordinate multiple conceptual frameworks, each with its own internal complexity (Stage 8-9), into
a functioning inter-framework whole. A multidisciplinary research program coordinates its
theoretical frameworks; an interdisciplinary curriculum coordinates its disciplinary frameworks;
a complex engineering project coordinates its domain-specific frameworks into one coherent design.

MHC Order 9 enables the coordination of multiple Order 8 frameworks into a complex framework
ecology where each framework retains its internal structure while participating in a larger
inter-framework coordination. The advance over Stage 9 is that the architecture now includes
*framework ecosystems* — not just one designed framework but a network of frameworks whose
coordination produces emergent explanatory power that no single framework was designed to produce.

## Integrity markers (healthy inclusion)

- **UL:** the felt complexity of operating within multiple overlapping framework contexts — the
  researcher who navigates multiple theoretical traditions simultaneously.
- **UR:** reliable inter-framework coordination that produces coherent explanatory power.
- **LL:** the shared scholarly culture that bridges framework boundaries — interdisciplinary
  norms, cross-field methodologies.
- **LR:** the inter-framework coordination mechanisms (interdisciplinary journals, cross-field
  conferences, unified theoretical models) as the external medium.

## Pathology markers (Agape / Eros)

- **Dark addiction:** inter-framework coordination that suppresses framework autonomy — the
  meta-framework becomes so dominant that individual frameworks lose their distinctive
  explanatory power.
- **Dark allergy:** failure to coordinate frameworks — the ecology is a collection of
  framework silos with no inter-framework intelligence.
- **Golden addiction:** claiming to reason about framework design as an abstract system
  (Stage 11) when actually just coordinating concrete frameworks.
- **Golden allergy:** refusing to recognize inter-framework coordination as genuine framework
  complexity because it is context-bound.

## Diagnostic cues (Gross / Ground R&D)

- **Multi-framework coordination:** the system reliably coordinates multiple frameworks, each
  with its own internal complexity.
- **Concrete-framework dependence:** coordination mechanisms are designed for specific,
  tangible disciplinary contexts, not abstract framework principles.
- **Framework ecosystem behavior:** the inter-framework system produces emergent explanatory
  power that no single framework was designed to produce.

## Sources, joints, open questions

**Sources:** Repko, *Interdisciplinary Research: Theory and Practice* (framework coordination);
Klein, *Mapping Interdisciplinary Studies* (framework ecology); National Research Council,
*Facilitating Interdisciplinary Research* (inter-framework institutional infrastructure).
**Open joints:** How does one distinguish genuine inter-framework coordination from mere
juxtaposition of frameworks?
**Research debt:** pairs with `09-primary-modern` (systematic framework construction) and
`11-abstract-emerge` (abstract framework analysis).
